title: Friend who couldn't afford the trip
author: Storytime
hook: On our girls trip, my friend said she couldn't afford anything, so we paid for her all week. On the last day, she showed us her bank account.
story: Five of us went to Mexico for my friend Dana's thirtieth. Our friend Mel said she was broke, but she really wanted to come. So we covered her. Her dinners. Her drinks. Her boat tour. By day three, people were annoyed. Two of the girls started a side group chat without her. I was in it. I'm not proud of what I wrote. Things like, she always does this, and next time she's not coming. On the last night, Mel asked us all to sit down. She opened her banking app and turned the phone around. There was more money in that account than I'll make in ten years. Her grandfather passed in the spring and left her almost everything. She said, I didn't want to be the rich friend. I wanted to see who would still want me around if I had nothing. Then she said she had booked a two week trip to Bali in January, fully paid, for anyone who'd been kind to her this week. Dana got a ticket. The girl who paid for her boat tour got a ticket. Then she looked at me, and slid her phone over again. It was a screenshot of the side group chat. Part two?
caption: I failed a test I didn't know I was taking 💸 #storytime
sound: a sunny, tropical beat that turns tense at very low volume
why: Group trip money drama splits viewers every time, the side group chat is the planted detail that comes back, and the screenshot ending is a strong part two hook.

title: Mother in law always gave me candles
author: Storytime
hook: Every Christmas, my mother-in-law gave everyone expensive gifts. Except me. I always got a candle.
story: My husband's mom, Diane, goes all out at Christmas. Designer bags for his sisters. A watch for my husband. And for me, every year, the same thing. A plain white candle. Handmade, she said. I never lit them. I put them in a box in the closet, five years of candles, and every year I cried in the car on the way home. I told my husband she hated me. He said she just wasn't good with words. Last week, our power went out during a storm. I couldn't find a flashlight, so I grabbed one of Diane's candles from the box and lit it. About an hour later, the wax melted down, and there was something inside. A tiny rolled up note, sealed in plastic. It said, I wasn't sure about you at first. I was wrong. I'm so glad my son found you. Dated five years ago. I lit the next one. Another note. And another. Every candle had one. The last one, from last Christmas, said, thank you for making him so happy. I hope you read these one day. Diane thinks I've been reading them all along. She thinks I just never mentioned it. How do I tell her I didn't?
caption: I should have lit them years ago 🕯️ #storytime
sound: a soft, warm Christmas piano at very low volume
why: Holiday gift season is starting, mother-in-law stories always pull engagement, the unlit candles are the setup, and the emotional twist makes people share and comment.

title: Dog walker on my doorbell camera
author: Storytime
hook: My dog walker was supposed to walk my dog for thirty minutes. My doorbell camera said they left for three hours.
story: I work long shifts, so I hired a dog walker through an app. A college student named Jordan. Thirty minutes a day, around the block, for my golden retriever, Biscuit. After a month, Biscuit started acting strange. He'd come home exhausted but happy. Smelling like perfume. And once, wearing a tiny knitted sweater. So I checked my doorbell camera. Jordan picked Biscuit up at noon and brought him back after three. Every single day. I was furious. I thought, what is this kid doing with my dog? The next day I took off work and followed them. Jordan drove Biscuit to a nursing home across town. I watched through the window. Biscuit walked from room to room, and old people lit up. One man who hadn't spoken in months was talking to him. The sweater was knitted by a ninety year old woman named Rose. Jordan's grandma lived there, and Jordan had been bringing Biscuit, without telling me, and without charging me the extra time. Here's the problem. Before I followed them, I had already reported Jordan to the app for stealing my dog. Jordan got banned. So what do I do now?
caption: I reported the wrong person 🐶 #storytime
sound: a gentle, heartwarming acoustic melody at very low volume
why: Pet stories reach a huge audience, the perfume and sweater are funny planted clues, and the guilt of the false report gives commenters something to advise on.
